mechanism_description: Metformin belongs to the class of Biguanide. Mechanism of Action: Inhibits hepatic gluconeogenesis via AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation and increases peripheral insulin sensitivity.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Metformin (Biguanide)
- **Clinical Indications:** Metabolic Syndrome, Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- **Target Symptoms:** Acanthosis Nigricans, Hyperglycemia, Insulin Resistance, Polyuria.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Inhibits hepatic gluconeogenesis via AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation and increases peripheral insulin sensitivity.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Gastrointestinal Upset, Lactic Acidosis, Metallic Taste, Vitamin B12 Deficiency.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020357; PMID:31548545; PMID:17924864; PMID:26900641; PMID:28938445.

mechanism_description: Semaglutide belongs to the class of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist. Mechanism of Action: Selectively binds and activates GLP-1 receptors, stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppressing glucagon.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Semaglutide (GLP-1 Receptor Agonist)
- **Clinical Indications:** Cardiovascular Disease in Diabetics, Obesity, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- **Target Symptoms:** Arterial Stiffness, Excess Adiposity, Hyperglycemia, Hyperphagia.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Selectively binds and activates GLP-1 receptors, stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppressing glucagon.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Constipation, Nausea, Pancreatitis Risk, Vomiting.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-BLA-125697; FDA-BLA-125697; PMID:34125345; PMID:33567185; PMID:38060356.

drug_class: Dual GIP and GLP-1 Receptor Agonist
mechanism_description: Tirzepatide belongs to the class of Dual GIP and GLP-1 Receptor Agonist. Mechanism of Action: Dual agonism of GIP and GLP-1 receptors synergistically enhances beta-cell insulin secretion and reduces glucagon levels.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Tirzepatide (Dual GIP and GLP-1 Receptor Agonist)
- **Clinical Indications:** Obesity, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- **Target Symptoms:** Excess Adiposity, Hyperglycemia.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Dual agonism of GIP and GLP-1 receptors synergistically enhances beta-cell insulin secretion and reduces glucagon levels.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Decreased Appetite, Diarrhea.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-215866; PMID:34170797; PMID:35658024.

indications: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
mechanism_description: Empagliflozin belongs to the class of SGLT2 Inhibitor. Mechanism of Action: Inhibits sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) in proximal renal tubules, inducing urinary excretion of glucose.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Empagliflozin (SGLT2 Inhibitor)
- **Clinical Indications:** Chronic Kidney Disease, Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- **Target Symptoms:** Dyspnea, Hyperglycemia, Proteinuria.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Inhibits sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) in proximal renal tubules, inducing urinary excretion of glucose.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Genital Mycotic Infections, Hypotension, Urinary Tract Infection.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-204629; PMID:26378978; PMID:32865377; PMID:36331190.

indications: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
mechanism_description: Dapagliflozin belongs to the class of SGLT2 Inhibitor. Mechanism of Action: Blocks proximal tubule glucose reabsorption independently of insulin secretion.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Dapagliflozin (SGLT2 Inhibitor)
- **Clinical Indications:** Chronic Kidney Disease, Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- **Target Symptoms:** Declining eGFR, Exercise Intolerance, Glucosuria.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Blocks proximal tubule glucose reabsorption independently of insulin secretion.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Euglycemic DKA, Polyuria, Volume Depletion.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-202293; PMID:24072873; PMID:32970396; PMID:36027572.

mechanism_description: Sitagliptin belongs to the class of DPP-4 Inhibitor. Mechanism of Action: Inhibits dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) degradation of endogenous incretins (GLP-1 and GIP).
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Sitagliptin (DPP-4 Inhibitor)
- **Clinical Indications:** Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- **Target Symptoms:** Hyperglycemia, Postprandial Hyperglycemia.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Inhibits dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) degradation of endogenous incretins (GLP-1 and GIP).
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Joint Pain, Nasopharyngitis.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-021995; PMID:17003251; PMID:26053366.

mechanism_description: Insulin Glargine belongs to the class of Long-Acting Basal Insulin. Mechanism of Action: Forms microprecipitates in subcutaneous tissue providing flat, peakless 24-hour basal insulin profile.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Insulin Glargine (Long-Acting Basal Insulin)
- **Clinical Indications:** Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- **Target Symptoms:** Fasting Hyperglycemia, Severe Hyperglycemia.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Forms microprecipitates in subcutaneous tissue providing flat, peakless 24-hour basal insulin profile.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Hypoglycemia, Lipodystrophy.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-BLA-021081; PMID:10868846; PMID:15616223.

mechanism_description: Glipizide belongs to the class of Second-Generation Sulfonylurea. Mechanism of Action: Closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels in pancreatic beta cells, triggering membrane depolarization and insulin release.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Glipizide (Second-Generation Sulfonylurea)
- **Clinical Indications:** Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- **Target Symptoms:** Hyperglycemia, Polyuria.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels in pancreatic beta cells, triggering membrane depolarization and insulin release.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Hypoglycemia, Weight Gain.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-017783; PMID:2661845; PMID:6219806.

mechanism_description: Lisinopril belongs to the class of ACE Inhibitor. Mechanism of Action: Competitively inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, preventing conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II and degrading bradykinin.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Lisinopril (ACE Inhibitor)
- **Clinical Indications:** Congestive Heart Failure, Diabetic Nephropathy, Essential Hypertension.
- **Target Symptoms:** Albuminuria, Elevated Blood Pressure, Peripheral Edema.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Competitively inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, preventing conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II and degrading bradykinin.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Angioedema, Dry Cough, Hyperkalemia.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-019777; PMID:2743129; PMID:10587334; PMID:8247036.

mechanism_description: Losartan belongs to the class of Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB). Mechanism of Action: Blocks the binding of angiotensin II to AT1 receptors in vascular smooth muscle and adrenal gland.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Losartan (Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB))
- **Clinical Indications:** Congestive Heart Failure, Diabetic Nephropathy, Essential Hypertension.
- **Target Symptoms:** Dyspnea on Exertion, Elevated Blood Pressure, Proteinuria.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Blocks the binding of angiotensin II to AT1 receptors in vascular smooth muscle and adrenal gland.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Dizziness, Hyperkalemia, Hypotension.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020386; PMID:7783335; PMID:10609816; PMID:11565518.

mechanism_description: Amlodipine belongs to the class of Dihydropyridine Calcium Channel Blocker. Mechanism of Action: Inhibits transmembrane influx of extracellular calcium ions across myocardial and vascular smooth muscle membranes.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Amlodipine (Dihydropyridine Calcium Channel Blocker)
- **Clinical Indications:** Chronic Stable Angina, Essential Hypertension, Vasospastic Angina.
- **Target Symptoms:** Chest Pain, Elevated Blood Pressure, Resting Angina.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Inhibits transmembrane influx of extracellular calcium ions across myocardial and vascular smooth muscle membranes.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Flushing, Headache, Peripheral Edema.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-019787; PMID:2528773; PMID:1936306; PMID:7523171.

mechanism_description: Atorvastatin belongs to the class of HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitor (Statin). Mechanism of Action: Competitively inhibits 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, upregulating hepatic LDL receptors.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Atorvastatin (HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitor (Statin))
- **Clinical Indications:** Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, Coronary Artery Disease, Hypercholesterolemia.
- **Target Symptoms:** Angina Pectoris, Elevated LDL-C, Vascular Plaque.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Competitively inhibits 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, upregulating hepatic LDL receptors.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Elevated Transaminases, Myalgia, Rhabdomyolysis Risk.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020702; PMID:9537248; PMID:11252182; PMID:15024479.

mechanism_description: Rosuvastatin belongs to the class of HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitor (Statin). Mechanism of Action: Hydrophilic statin with high selectivity for hepatic HMG-CoA reductase and low passive membrane permeability in muscle.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Rosuvastatin (HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitor (Statin))
- **Clinical Indications:** Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, Hypercholesterolemia.
- **Target Symptoms:** Elevated LDL-C, Elevated hs-CRP.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Hydrophilic statin with high selectivity for hepatic HMG-CoA reductase and low passive membrane permeability in muscle.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Myalgia, Proteinuria.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-021366; PMID:14564343; PMID:18997196.

indications: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
mechanism_description: Metoprolol belongs to the class of Beta-1 Selective Adrenergic Antagonist. Mechanism of Action: Selectively antagonizes beta-1 adrenergic receptors in cardiac tissue, reducing heart rate and cardiac output.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Metoprolol (Beta-1 Selective Adrenergic Antagonist)
- **Clinical Indications:** Angina Pectoris, Essential Hypertension, Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
- **Target Symptoms:** Elevated Blood Pressure, Exertional Chest Tightness, Tachycardia.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Selectively antagonizes beta-1 adrenergic receptors in cardiac tissue, reducing heart rate and cardiac output.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Bradycardia, Erectile Dysfunction, Fatigue.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-019974; PMID:6337583; PMID:10376614; PMID:3890886.

mechanism_description: Carvedilol belongs to the class of Nonselective Beta and Alpha-1 Blocker. Mechanism of Action: Combines nonselective beta-adrenergic blockade with alpha-1 receptor-mediated peripheral vasodilation.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Carvedilol (Nonselective Beta and Alpha-1 Blocker)
- **Clinical Indications:** Congestive Heart Failure, Essential Hypertension.
- **Target Symptoms:** Dyspnea on Exertion, Elevated Blood Pressure.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Combines nonselective beta-adrenergic blockade with alpha-1 receptor-mediated peripheral vasodilation.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Dizziness, Orthostatic Hypotension.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020297; PMID:8622127; PMID:11434351.

mechanism_description: Apixaban belongs to the class of Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC). Mechanism of Action: Directly and reversibly inhibits free and clot-bound Factor Xa, suppressing prothrombinase activity.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Apixaban (Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC))
- **Clinical Indications:** Atrial Fibrillation, Deep Vein Thrombosis, Pulmonary Embolism.
- **Target Symptoms:** Lower Limb Swelling, Palpitations, Pleuritic Chest Pain.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Directly and reversibly inhibits free and clot-bound Factor Xa, suppressing prothrombinase activity.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Bruising, Gastrointestinal Bleed, Major Bleeding.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-202155; PMID:21870978; PMID:23447955; PMID:23812891.

mechanism_description: Warfarin belongs to the class of Vitamin K Antagonist. Mechanism of Action: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1), preventing gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Warfarin (Vitamin K Antagonist)
- **Clinical Indications:** Atrial Fibrillation, Prosthetic Heart Valve Thrombosis.
- **Target Symptoms:** Irregular Pulse, Thromboembolism.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1), preventing gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Severe Hemorrhage, Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-009218; PMID:14966050; PMID:8192667.

mechanism_description: Albuterol belongs to the class of Short-Acting Beta-2 Agonist (SABA). Mechanism of Action: Stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors on airway smooth muscle, activating adenylate cyclase and relaxing bronchial smooth muscle.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Albuterol (Short-Acting Beta-2 Agonist (SABA))
- **Clinical Indications:** Asthma, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
- **Target Symptoms:** Dyspnea, Shortness of Breath, Wheezing.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors on airway smooth muscle, activating adenylate cyclase and relaxing bronchial smooth muscle.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Palpitations, Tachycardia, Tremor.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-019489; PMID:11738517; PMID:15961603; PMID:8482431.

mechanism_description: Fluticasone belongs to the class of Inhaled Corticosteroid. Mechanism of Action: Translocates into the nucleus to inhibit transcription factors NF-kB and AP-1, suppressing cytokine synthesis.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Fluticasone (Inhaled Corticosteroid)
- **Clinical Indications:** Allergic Rhinitis, Asthma, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
- **Target Symptoms:** Airway Inflammation, Frequent Exacerbations, Rhinorrhea.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Translocates into the nucleus to inhibit transcription factors NF-kB and AP-1, suppressing cytokine synthesis.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Dysphonia, Epistaxis, Oral Candidiasis.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-021433; PMID:9577937; PMID:10724300; PMID:17314337.

mechanism_description: Budesonide belongs to the class of Inhaled / Gut-Targeted Glucocorticoid. Mechanism of Action: Exerts high local glucocorticoid receptor affinity with extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism limiting systemic bioavailability.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Budesonide (Inhaled / Gut-Targeted Glucocorticoid)
- **Clinical Indications:** Asthma, Crohn's Disease.
- **Target Symptoms:** Ileal Inflammation, Nocturnal Cough.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Exerts high local glucocorticoid receptor affinity with extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism limiting systemic bioavailability.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Cushingoid Features, Throat Irritation.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020929; PMID:10793786; PMID:15846624.

mechanism_description: Montelukast belongs to the class of Leukotriene Receptor Antagonist. Mechanism of Action: Selectively antagonizes cysteinyl leukotriene CysLT1 receptors, blocking LTD4-induced airway smooth muscle spasm.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Montelukast (Leukotriene Receptor Antagonist)
- **Clinical Indications:** Allergic Rhinitis, Asthma.
- **Target Symptoms:** Bronchoconstriction, Nasal Congestion.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Selectively antagonizes cysteinyl leukotriene CysLT1 receptors, blocking LTD4-induced airway smooth muscle spasm.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Headache, Neuropsychiatric Events.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020829; PMID:9876274; PMID:11827474.

mechanism_description: Sertraline belongs to the class of Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI). Mechanism of Action: Potently inhibits serotonin transporter (SERT) reuptake, enhancing synaptic 5-HT availability.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Sertraline (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI))
- **Clinical Indications:** Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder.
- **Target Symptoms:** Anhedonia, Excessive Worry, Flashbacks, Intrusive Thoughts.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Potently inhibits serotonin transporter (SERT) reuptake, enhancing synaptic 5-HT availability.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Insomnia, Nausea, Sexual Dysfunction, Tremor.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-019839; PMID:1603096; PMID:10757755; PMID:12401735; PMID:8601362.

mechanism_description: Escitalopram belongs to the class of Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI). Mechanism of Action: Pure S-enantiomer exhibiting allosteric serotonin transporter binding with high target selectivity.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Escitalopram (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI))
- **Clinical Indications:** Major Depressive Disorder, Panic Disorder.
- **Target Symptoms:** Depressed Mood, Panic Attacks.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Pure S-enantiomer exhibiting allosteric serotonin transporter binding with high target selectivity.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Somnolence, Sweating.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-021323; PMID:12044195; PMID:15055233.

mechanism_description: Duloxetine belongs to the class of Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitor (SNRI). Mechanism of Action: Dual inhibition of neuronal serotonin (SERT) and norepinephrine (NET) reuptake transporters.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Duloxetine (Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitor (SNRI))
- **Clinical Indications:** Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathic Pain, Fibromyalgia, Major Depressive Disorder.
- **Target Symptoms:** Burning Neuropathic Pain, Diffuse Musculoskeletal Pain, Psychomotor Retardation.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Dual inhibition of neuronal serotonin (SERT) and norepinephrine (NET) reuptake transporters.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Constipation, Dry Mouth, Nausea.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-021427; PMID:15234909; PMID:16140730; PMID:18497676.

mechanism_description: Levodopa belongs to the class of Dopamine Precursor. Mechanism of Action: Crosses the blood-brain barrier via large neutral amino acid transporter (LAT1) and decarboxylates into dopamine.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Levodopa (Dopamine Precursor)
- **Clinical Indications:** Parkinson's Disease.
- **Target Symptoms:** Bradykinesia, Muscle Rigidity, Resting Tremor.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Crosses the blood-brain barrier via large neutral amino acid transporter (LAT1) and decarboxylates into dopamine.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Dyskinesia, Orthostatic Hypotension, Visual Hallucinations.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-016834; PMID:5417436; PMID:11986445; PMID:15610816.

mechanism_description: Donepezil belongs to the class of Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitor. Mechanism of Action: Reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, prolonging the action of acetylcholine at central cholinergic synapses.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Donepezil (Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitor)
- **Clinical Indications:** Alzheimer's Disease.
- **Target Symptoms:** Cognitive Decline, Memory Loss.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, prolonging the action of acetylcholine at central cholinergic synapses.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Bradycardia, Diarrhea.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020655; PMID:9786431; PMID:11346369.

mechanism_description: Memantine belongs to the class of NMDA Receptor Antagonist. Mechanism of Action: Uncompetitive, low-affinity NMDA open-channel blocker that prevents excitotoxic glutamate signaling.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Memantine (NMDA Receptor Antagonist)
- **Clinical Indications:** Alzheimer's Disease.
- **Target Symptoms:** Disorientation, Severe Cognitive Impairment.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Uncompetitive, low-affinity NMDA open-channel blocker that prevents excitotoxic glutamate signaling.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Confusion, Dizziness.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-021487; PMID:12672858; PMID:15649964.

mechanism_description: Gabapentin belongs to the class of Alpha-2-Delta Ligand. Mechanism of Action: Binds high-affinity alpha-2-delta auxiliary subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels, attenuating neurotransmitter exocytosis.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Gabapentin (Alpha-2-Delta Ligand)
- **Clinical Indications:** Focal Seizures, Neuropathic Pain, Postherpetic Neuralgia.
- **Target Symptoms:** Allodynia, Hyperalgesia, Involuntary Muscle Spasms.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Binds high-affinity alpha-2-delta auxiliary subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels, attenuating neurotransmitter exocytosis.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Dizziness, Peripheral Edema, Somnolence.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020235; PMID:9847116; PMID:8243144; PMID:9851887.

mechanism_description: Pregabalin belongs to the class of Alpha-2-Delta Ligand. Mechanism of Action: High-affinity modulator of P/Q-type calcium channel trafficking, reducing excitatory spinal neurotransmitter release.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Pregabalin (Alpha-2-Delta Ligand)
- **Clinical Indications:** Fibromyalgia, Neuropathic Pain.
- **Target Symptoms:** Burning Sensation, Widespread Pain.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** High-affinity modulator of P/Q-type calcium channel trafficking, reducing excitatory spinal neurotransmitter release.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Ataxia, Weight Gain.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-021446; PMID:15234911; PMID:18497679.

mechanism_description: Sumatriptan belongs to the class of 5-HT1B/1D Receptor Agonist (Triptan). Mechanism of Action: Constricts meningeal and cerebral blood vessels via 5-HT1B receptors and inhibits trigeminal sensory nerve activation via 5-HT1D receptors.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Sumatriptan (5-HT1B/1D Receptor Agonist (Triptan))
- **Clinical Indications:** Cluster Headache, Migraine.
- **Target Symptoms:** Periorbital Piercing Pain, Photophobia, Unilateral Throbbing Headache.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Constricts meningeal and cerebral blood vessels via 5-HT1B receptors and inhibits trigeminal sensory nerve activation via 5-HT1D receptors.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Chest Tightness, Coronary Vasospasm Risk, Paresthesia.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020080; PMID:1653139; PMID:18070094; PMID:8243149.

mechanism_description: Methotrexate belongs to the class of Antifolate DMARD. Mechanism of Action: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and aminoimidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase, leading to extracellular adenosine accumulation.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Methotrexate (Antifolate DMARD)
- **Clinical Indications:** Plaque Psoriasis, Psoriatic Arthritis, Rheumatoid Arthritis.
- **Target Symptoms:** Dactylitis, Erythematous Scaly Plaques, Joint Pain and Swelling.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and aminoimidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase, leading to extracellular adenosine accumulation.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Bone Marrow Suppression, Hepatotoxicity, Stomatitis.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-011719; PMID:15234909; PMID:10724305; PMID:12702061.

mechanism_description: Adalimumab belongs to the class of Anti-TNF Monoclonal Antibody. Mechanism of Action: Specifically binds soluble and membrane-bound TNF-alpha, preventing interaction with p55 and p75 cell surface receptors.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Adalimumab (Anti-TNF Monoclonal Antibody)
- **Clinical Indications:** Ankylosing Spondylitis, Crohn's Disease, Rheumatoid Arthritis, Ulcerative Colitis.
- **Target Symptoms:** Abdominal Pain, Bloody Diarrhea, Inflammatory Back Pain, Morning Joint Stiffness.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Specifically binds soluble and membrane-bound TNF-alpha, preventing interaction with p55 and p75 cell surface receptors.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Demyelinating Disease Risk, Injection Site Reaction, Serious Infection Risk, Tuberculosis Reactivation Risk.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-BLA-125057; PMID:12687508; PMID:16531398; PMID:17298758; PMID:22266897.

mechanism_description: Infliximab belongs to the class of Chimeric Anti-TNF Monoclonal Antibody. Mechanism of Action: High-affinity binding of soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha, lysing target cells via complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Infliximab (Chimeric Anti-TNF Monoclonal Antibody)
- **Clinical Indications:** Crohn's Disease, Rheumatoid Arthritis.
- **Target Symptoms:** Fistula Formation, Synovial Proliferation.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** High-affinity binding of soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha, lysing target cells via complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Infusion Reactions, Opportunistic Fungal Infections.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-BLA-103772; PMID:9321530; PMID:10609819.

indications: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
mechanism_description: Pembrolizumab belongs to the class of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (PD-1 Blocker). Mechanism of Action: Selectively binds PD-1 receptor on cytotoxic T-cells, preventing engagement with PD-L1/PD-L2 and reactivating antitumor immunity.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Pembrolizumab (Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (PD-1 Blocker))
- **Clinical Indications:** Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Melanoma, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
- **Target Symptoms:** Hemoptysis, Malignant Skin Lesion, Neck Mass.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Selectively binds PD-1 receptor on cytotoxic T-cells, preventing engagement with PD-L1/PD-L2 and reactivating antitumor immunity.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Immune-Mediated Colitis, Immune-Mediated Pneumonitis, Thyroiditis.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-BLA-125514; PMID:25891304; PMID:27718847; PMID:31679945.

mechanism_description: Imatinib belongs to the class of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (BCR-ABL). Mechanism of Action: Competitively binds ATP-binding pocket of BCR-ABL oncoprotein, arresting leukemic cell proliferation.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Imatinib (Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (BCR-ABL))
- **Clinical Indications:** Chronic Myeloid Leukemia, Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor.
- **Target Symptoms:** Abdominal Mass, Splenomegaly.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Competitively binds ATP-binding pocket of BCR-ABL oncoprotein, arresting leukemic cell proliferation.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Fluid Retention, Nausea.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-021335; PMID:11287951; PMID:11932470.

mechanism_description: Tamoxifen belongs to the class of Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM). Mechanism of Action: Competitively antagonizes estrogen binding to estrogen receptors in mammary gland tissue.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Tamoxifen (Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM))
- **Clinical Indications:** Breast Cancer (ER-Positive).
- **Target Symptoms:** Breast Lump, Nipple Discharge.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Competitively antagonizes estrogen binding to estrogen receptors in mammary gland tissue.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Hot Flashes, Thromboembolism Risk.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-017970; PMID:9786435; PMID:10376618.

mechanism_description: Omeprazole belongs to the class of Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI). Mechanism of Action: Covalently binds cysteine residues of H+/K+ ATPase in gastric parietal cells, shutting down basal and stimulated gastric acid production.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Omeprazole (Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI))
- **Clinical Indications:** Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome.
- **Target Symptoms:** Epigastric Pain, Heartburn, Severe Hyperacidity.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Covalently binds cysteine residues of H+/K+ ATPase in gastric parietal cells, shutting down basal and stimulated gastric acid production.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Bone Fracture Risk, Clostridium difficile Infection Risk, Hypomagnesemia.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-019810; PMID:2167448; PMID:1709405; PMID:24072879.

mechanism_description: Pantoprazole belongs to the class of Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI). Mechanism of Action: Selective binding to Cys822 of proton pump with low CYP2C19 interaction potential.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Pantoprazole (Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI))
- **Clinical Indications:** Erosive Esophagitis, Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease.
- **Target Symptoms:** Acid Regurgitation, Odynophagia.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Selective binding to Cys822 of proton pump with low CYP2C19 interaction potential.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Diarrhea, Headache.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020987; PMID:10793789; PMID:12401739.

mechanism_description: Amoxicillin belongs to the class of Aminopenicillin Antibiotic. Mechanism of Action: Inactivates penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) involved in peptidoglycan crosslinking, triggering osmotic bacterial cell lysis.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Amoxicillin (Aminopenicillin Antibiotic)
- **Clinical Indications:** Acute Otitis Media, Community-Acquired Pneumonia, Streptococcal Pharyngitis.
- **Target Symptoms:** Otalgia, Productive Cough, Sore Throat.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Inactivates penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) involved in peptidoglycan crosslinking, triggering osmotic bacterial cell lysis.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Allergic Anaphylaxis, Diarrhea, Maculopapular Rash.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-050542; PMID:6390822; PMID:11520976; PMID:17924869.

mechanism_description: Ciprofloxacin belongs to the class of Fluoroquinolone Antibiotic. Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, causing double-stranded DNA breaks and bactericidal death.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Ciprofloxacin (Fluoroquinolone Antibiotic)
- **Clinical Indications:** Acute Pyelonephritis, Complicated Urinary Tract Infection, Infectious Diarrhea.
- **Target Symptoms:** Abdominal Cramps, Dysuria, Flank Pain.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, causing double-stranded DNA breaks and bactericidal death.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** CNS Toxicity, QT Prolongation, Tendon Rupture Risk.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-019537; PMID:2890458; PMID:10587339; PMID:3300588.

mechanism_description: Doxycycline belongs to the class of Tetracycline Antibiotic. Mechanism of Action: Reversibly binds the 30S ribosomal subunit, preventing aminoacyl-tRNA association and halting bacterial protein synthesis.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Doxycycline (Tetracycline Antibiotic)
- **Clinical Indications:** Acne Vulgaris, Community-Acquired Pneumonia, Lyme Disease.
- **Target Symptoms:** Erythema Migrans, Fever and Chills, Inflammatory Papules.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Reversibly binds the 30S ribosomal subunit, preventing aminoacyl-tRNA association and halting bacterial protein synthesis.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Esophageal Irritation, Photosensitivity, Tooth Discoloration (Children).
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-050444; PMID:9208447; PMID:11986449; PMID:17518471.

mechanism_description: Azithromycin belongs to the class of Macrolide Antibiotic. Mechanism of Action: Reversibly binds to 50S ribosomal subunit, preventing peptide translocation during bacterial protein elongation.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Azithromycin (Macrolide Antibiotic)
- **Clinical Indications:** Acute Bacterial Sinusitis, Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
- **Target Symptoms:** Facial Pain, Shortness of Breath.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Reversibly binds to 50S ribosomal subunit, preventing peptide translocation during bacterial protein elongation.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Diarrhea, QT Interval Prolongation.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-050670; PMID:8482436; PMID:11738521.

mechanism_description: Paxlovid belongs to the class of Viral Protease Inhibitor. Mechanism of Action: Nirmatrelvir potently inhibits SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro/3CLpro); ritonavir acts as a pharmacokinetic booster via CYP3A inhibition.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Paxlovid (Viral Protease Inhibitor)
- **Clinical Indications:** COVID-19.
- **Target Symptoms:** Cough, Fever, Loss of Taste or Smell.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Nirmatrelvir potently inhibits SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro/3CLpro); ritonavir acts as a pharmacokinetic booster via CYP3A inhibition.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** CYP3A Drug-Drug Interactions, Dysgeusia (Metallic Taste), Elevated Blood Pressure.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-EUA-106; PMID:35172054; PMID:35172054; PMID:35472899.

mechanism_description: Ibuprofen belongs to the class of Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug (NSAID). Mechanism of Action: Nonselectively inhibits cyclooxygenase isoforms COX-1 and COX-2, decreasing prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) synthesis.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Ibuprofen (Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug (NSAID))
- **Clinical Indications:** Osteoarthritis, Tension Headache.
- **Target Symptoms:** Constricting Head Pain, Joint Stiffness.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Nonselectively inhibits cyclooxygenase isoforms COX-1 and COX-2, decreasing prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) synthesis.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Gastric Ulceration, Renal Impairment.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-017463; PMID:3890889; PMID:8247039.

mechanism_description: Celecoxib belongs to the class of Selective COX-2 Inhibitor. Mechanism of Action: Selectively inhibits cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) sparing platelet COX-1, reducing inflammatory prostanoids without gastrointestinal ulceration.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Celecoxib (Selective COX-2 Inhibitor)
- **Clinical Indications:** Ankylosing Spondylitis, Osteoarthritis.
- **Target Symptoms:** Joint Crepitus, Spinal Rigidity.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Selectively inhibits cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) sparing platelet COX-1, reducing inflammatory prostanoids without gastrointestinal ulceration.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Cardiovascular Thrombotic Risk, Fluid Retention.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-020998; PMID:10499703; PMID:11565522.

mechanism_description: Colchicine belongs to the class of Microtubule Disassembly Inhibitor. Mechanism of Action: Binds tubulin heterodimers preventing microtubule polymer assembly, blocking neutrophil chemotaxis and NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
pharmacology_summary:
### Monograph: Colchicine (Microtubule Disassembly Inhibitor)
- **Clinical Indications:** Gout Flares, Pericarditis.
- **Target Symptoms:** Positional Chest Pain, Severe Podagra.
- **Pharmacological Action & Pathway:** Binds tubulin heterodimers preventing microtubule polymer assembly, blocking neutrophil chemotaxis and NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
- **Known Adverse Reactions & Warnings:** Abdominal Cramping, Severe Diarrhea.
- **Evidence & Citations:** FDA-NDA-022352; PMID:20444988; PMID:24072881.
